evidence: The reviewer admitted it could not run rustc and argued only from the absence of bare String fields; the agent cited tracing-core field.rs's `impl Value for String`, a passing cargo build/test on that commit, and a rendered log line `language="es"`, and every later round's suite (190 passed) ran with the same field unchanged.

next_event takes only a VecDeque and an mpsc receiver, so the drain-order contract was testable without a room, and lib.rs had no test module; 7283e05 added three tests for backlog-first, event-survives-drain and closed-room. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted the finding and added the tests.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces an ordering guarantee in a function with plain inputs (a queue and a receiver), add the contract test in the same commit instead of deciding it only tests the language.

evidence: The agent confirmed that no test named `languages_travel_as_their_published_codes` exists; the real one is `closed_vocabularies_match_their_published_names` at fixtures.rs:629. Fixed in 6d8acca.
guidance_note: Before a doc comment names a test or function as the guarantee, grep for that exact identifier.

evidence: The hunk shows `told = present` is assigned synchronously, before the publishes settle, so an agent whose publish failed was never retried. The agent's 96f8603 moved the write into each publish's fulfilment arm. That was right for the stated bug, but it opened the overlapping-sweep window that F10 and F11 found.
guidance_note: When moving a record's write from 'at start' to 'on settle', name the in-between state and check whether two concurrent callers can both see it as absent; the caller.js comment already said the open sweep and the arrival handler overlap.

evidence: This same PR added a second caller of `code()` in web.rs:140 (`Language::ALL.iter().map(|language| language.code())`), so the doc's claim of 'a log line written once per conversation' was false. The agent deleted the sentence instead of listing call sites.
guidance_note: Don't put call-site counts or frequencies in a function doc; they go stale the moment the same PR adds a caller.

evidence: `this.configuring = this.configuring.then(...)` with no rejection arm does stop every later arrived() call after one failure. The reviewer's `.catch(() => {})` would swallow the failure that the handler comment says must stay fatal, so the agent replaced the chain with a list of independent attempts awaited by Promise.all.
guidance_note: Don't sequence independent attempts through one promise chain; keep each attempt as its own promise so one rejection cannot stop the others.

evidence: `await this.configuring` was the only unbounded wait among the module's room operations; the others race rejectAfter. Accepting was right, but the fix raced a second `rejectAfter(ms)` after a `waitFor(ms)`. The round-5 finding recovered from the run log (issue comment, item 2) shows this let the call take up to 2×ms, which was fixed later in 0a66791.
guidance_note: When bounding a second phase of a call that already takes a budget, draw both phases from one deadline (`until = now + ms`) rather than giving each a fresh `ms`.

evidence: The agent's own acceptance output showed `ok  the agent is a connected participant` while its six sibling scripts say '...holds this conversation's configuration'. Relabelled in 6d8acca.
guidance_note: When a mechanical edit changes what a check asserts in N scripts, grep for the old label across all N before committing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7283e05 only added a test module to lib.rs. The greeting replay comes from the original PR's full-snapshot `conversationInitiation`, which the agent traced end to end (app.js:445 → everyone() → lib.rs:526). The agent took the reviewer's second option, the agent-side `opening_after`, but changed only how often the arm fires. Its own reply named the orphaned-token mechanism and left it in place, and F12 then found it.
guidance_note: When a reply names a worse underlying mechanism (an assignment that orphans a cancellation token), fix that mechanism in the same commit rather than only reducing how often it fires.

evidence: Before F4's fix (96f8603), `told = present` was written synchronously, so overlapping sweeps could not both publish; moving the write into the fulfilment arm opened the window. The flagged commit a521274 is the F9 fix and does not touch this code. The agent confirmed the overlap is reachable via the SDK's emitWhenConnected buffering and replaced the in-flight-set suggestion with a Map of identity to pending publish (5b30a54), which also lets a second sweep wait on the first.
guidance_note: Before committing a fix that defers a record write, write the overlapping-callers test (a publish held open by hand) that the repo's own caller.js comment says is the ordinary case.

evidence: This is the same duplicate-publish window as F10, reached through caller.js's reportPresence; it was opened when 96f8603 moved `told` to on-settle. The reviewer was unsure the event can fire during connect; the agent showed the vendored bundle's `emitWhenConnected(_.ParticipantConnected, n)` buffers it. The fix went into conversation.js, which owns the record, instead of the in-flight set the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: Fix a race in the module that owns the shared record, not at one of its callers, so every caller that overlaps is covered.

evidence: a521274 (the F9 fix) only changed `if let Some(greeting) = opening`, and the arm still did `answering = Some(start_turn(...))` over a token that does not cancel on drop. The agent's F9 reply had already named this orphaning as the real cost. The flagged commit 5b30a54 only touched conversation.js. The agent added stop_answering in 50db7f8 and verified it on a live call.
guidance_note: When a fix narrows when a buggy arm runs, check whether the arm is still wrong when it does run; here the remaining legitimate trigger still orphaned the turn.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the JSDoc citing client.rs's 'tts and conversation routinely arrive as empty objects' is already in the round-1 F9 hunk, and 5b30a54 changed only conversationWith. `conversationInitiation` builds only agent and tts, so the cited justification overstated what the function mirrors. The agent took the reviewer's second option and fixed the comment, not the payload.
guidance_note: When a comment justifies a shape by citing another file, check that the shape actually matches every part of what is cited.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: folding connect and configure into `open()` inside Call.join is in the original PR (the round-0 hunk shows `await conversation.open(`), and 5b30a54 did not change it. The agent confirmed that master had `await reportPresence().catch(reportDetached)` with a written rationale. The fix took the reviewer's first option, a separate catch, made structural with a typed `NotTold`.
guidance_note: When consolidating two callers' sequences into one shared function, carry over each caller's documented per-step failure policy (here 'a configure that fails costs the voice, not the call') before deleting the old code.

evidence: 6581008 replaced `stop_answering` with `Answering::start/stop`, but the session.rs doc written in a521274 still says a turn 'is only ever cancelled through `stop_answering`' and is orphaned. 6581008 answered the round-6 log-recovered finding that followed up F12's fix; that finding has no id, so it is attributed here to F12. The thread was resolved with no reply. It is marked outdated, which suggests a later change, but the packet does not show one.
guidance_note: When a refactor renames or removes a function, grep the whole repo for the old name in comments, especially ones that explain a bug in terms of that function.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 6581008 touched only lib.rs, and `Promise.all(identities.map(...))` in `tell` predates review (it is in the pre-5b30a54 code). The bug is real, since Promise.all surfaces only the first rejection and the comment promises that 'a failure names the agent'. It is latent, though: the reviewer notes one agent identity per conversation in practice. The thread was resolved silently and the packet does not show whether it changed.
guidance_note: When a comment promises that each failure is named, use allSettled and aggregate rather than Promise.all, which reports only the first.

evidence: F14's fix (50db7f8) introduced NotTold and tested the browser-side keep-the-call path, but nothing pins the node-side opposite contract that `Caller.join()` must reject. The flagged commit 6581008 is lib.rs only; the real origin is F14's fix. An earlier issue comment had dismissed testing `join()` as structure, but this asks for a behavioral contract. The thread was resolved with no reply.
guidance_note: When a fix gives two callers opposite policies for one typed failure, test both policies, not only the one being changed.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 6581008 is lib.rs only, and agentConfigured's success path has had no unit test since the original PR; the `callerAwaiting` fixture seeds `configuring: [new Promise(() => {})]`, so it can only reject. The premise is only partly right because every acceptance run (agent 10/10 and so on) exercises the success path live. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated, so nothing was recorded or changed.
guidance_note: When writing a fixture that can only reach the failure branch, add the matching success-path case beside it.

narrative: This is a large handshake-consolidation PR that hit the 5-round review cap. Round 2 was entirely fix-caused: F4's fix moved the `told` write to on-settle, which reopened a duplicate-publish race (F10, F11). F9's fix (opening_after) reduced how often a greeting orphaned a running turn but left the arm orphaning, even though the agent's own reply named the orphaning mechanism; that produced F12, and the later Answering refactor left a comment naming the deleted stop_answering (F15). F7's bounded-wait fix doubled the budget, which a log-recovered round-5 finding caught. Most round-0 decisions, including pushing back on the tracing String finding and the different fixes for F6 and F10, were correct and well verified.
guidance_observations: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the deeper mechanism in a plan reply (orphaned token, three-state record) but fixed only the narrower symptom first, so a later round had to come back for the rest.
Four round-4 threads were resolved with no reply, so whether F15-F18 were fixed is unrecorded on the PR.
Log-recovered findings from crashed review rounds were answered in issue comments without finding ids, which breaks traceability of the F7 and F12 follow-ups.

evidence: `.gitea/workflows/publish-image.yaml:21-22` still said GitHub 'cannot reach this network', contradicting the rewrite's 'can be joined ... we refuse it'. The agent took the reviewer's first option and corrected the workflow comment in 170e0cb; it checked that only comment lines changed and that the parsed YAML was identical.
guidance_note: When a PR exists to remove a false claim, grep the repo for the same claim in other files, starting with the file the edited doc points readers to.

evidence: The rewrite copied a detailed Cloudflare enumeration from another repo's file into CLAUDE.md, where nothing re-checks it. The agent replaced the copy with the rule plus a pointer to `home-infra/CLAUDE.md:11`, matching the argument this file already makes about provenance labels.
guidance_note: When citing another repo's policy, state the rule and point at the source instead of transcribing the specifics.

evidence: The agent's grep found 'nomad' only in prose at publish-image.yaml:309-310; the publish job talks only to $REGISTRY. 'and Nomad access' overstated the build's credentials and was removed in 170e0cb.
guidance_note: Before stating what credentials a build needs, read the workflow's actual steps.

narrative: This is a one-paragraph doc rewrite. Round 0 raised three valid findings: a contradiction with the workflow comment, an over-transcribed external policy, and an inflated Nomad-credential claim. All three were accepted and fixed in one commit, and round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: All three findings were things a pre-push check of the files the doc points to (the workflow) would have caught.

evidence: The budget is calibrated only on ggml-base.en while the model is configurable, so a heavier accelerated model is refused. The reviewer offered 'scale with, or be documented as tied to'; the agent took the documentation half and made the failure message name the model cause. It argued that a self-scaling budget could never fail, which is a sound reason for the fixed constant.
guidance_note: When a threshold is calibrated against one configuration that operators can change, say so at the constant and in the error message from the start.

evidence: 85ms is not in the table, and the stated margins only work from 56ms. The agent's plan rejected 56ms in favour of CUDA's 84ms, then measured and found that 84ms was itself a first-call figure (warm CUDA is 41ms), so 56ms was right after all. The final commit 47e48a7 matched the reviewer and also corrected the table's data.
guidance_note: Confirm every figure in a calibration table was measured under the condition the check uses (warm) before deriving margins from it, and before using the table to argue against a reviewer.

evidence: Both warm-up calls map into `TranscribeError::Warmup`, so 'failed its first run' became wrong once the PR added the second call. The agent reworded it to 'failed its warm-up', the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: When adding a second call that maps to an existing error variant, re-read that variant's Display text.

evidence: The SlowInference message stated backend-init failure as fact while the function's own doc named an oversized model as a second cause. The agent rewrote the message to name both causes. It did not update the variant doc or the function doc with the same framing, and F5 and F6 then found each of those.
guidance_note: When correcting what an error means, update every description of it in the same commit: the Display arm, the variant doc and the doc of the function that returns it.

evidence: The agent says so itself: 'it is the unfinished half of an earlier finding'. F4's fix gave the Display message two causes and left the variant doc saying 'the same image on the same host starts healthy', which is purely transient. The flagged commit 47e48a7 changed only the calibration table and tests, so the drift comes from F4's message fix. Reworded in 4ac9ada.
guidance_note: After changing an error's described causes, grep the variant name and update every doc comment that describes it.

evidence: 4ac9ada (the F5 fix) updated only the variant doc. `require_fast_inference`'s doc still opened with 'the third and last way to lose the GPU', the single cause, which is the third copy of the fact that the F4 and F5 fixes each missed. The agent named the pattern ('third round on one fact') and reframed the doc around inference speed in a730475.
guidance_note: When a second reviewer round finds another stale copy of the same fact, sweep for all remaining copies before pushing instead of fixing only the one cited.

narrative: This PR adds a warm-inference latency check. Round 0's four findings were valid: a model-size false refusal, a wrong calibration figure, a stale run count and a single-cause error message. The fix for the single-cause message updated only the Display arm, so rounds 1 and 2 each found one more prose copy of 'what produces SlowInference', the variant doc and then the function doc. On F2 the agent first argued against the reviewer using a number that was itself wrong, then measured and conceded.
guidance_observations: Rounds 1 and 2 existed only because a change to an error's meaning was applied to one of its three prose descriptions at a time.
Measuring on real hardware before writing the calibration fix was the right move, but the agent's plan reply argued from unverified data first.
